current_answer: Interledger Foundation’s 2026 Local Impact Mini-Grants accept rolling applications through 11 November from registered or unregistered groups and individual practitioners worldwide, subject to United States sanctions restrictions. Awards range from USD 500 to USD 3,000 for a concrete local project on open payments, digital financial access, open-source innovation, financial inclusion, or digital public infrastructure. This is direct project funding, not general salary or startup runway: the issuer excludes general operating expenses and capital expenditures.

catalogue_card.question: Up to USD 3,000 is open. Does your local fintech project fit the remit?
catalogue_card.text: Interledger Foundation accepts rolling applications through 11 November for USD 500–3,000 in direct project funding. Individuals, unregistered groups, and local fintech startups can apply from any geography subject to United States sanctions restrictions. The project must serve open payments or digital financial access. A short form, two-page concept note, budget, and timeline are required; selection and payment terms are not published.

summary: Interledger Foundation lists USD 500–3,000 for a concrete local project and accepts rolling applications through 11 November 2026.
Registered or unregistered organisations and individual practitioners, including local fintech startups, may apply from any geography subject to United States sanctions restrictions.
The work must concern open payments, digital financial access, open-source innovation, financial inclusion, or digital public infrastructure.
The application requires a short form, two-page concept note, budget, and timeline. Projects must finish within six months of acceptance.

Direct project activities are eligible; general operating expenses and capital expenditures are excluded. The issuer does not publish a typical award, selection rate, award guarantee, payment terms, or a promised decision time.
uncertainty: Interledger does not publish a selection rate, typical award, or award guarantee; its two-week follow-up statement is not a decision promise.

The published page lists project-specific facilitator compensation and organizer stipends but excludes general operating expenses, including organizer compensation; confirm any budget line in the live application materials.
